text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x holds Taiwanese citizenship.

Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
∀x (CitizenUS(x) → CanRegister(x)) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (CitizenUS(x) ∨ CitizenTaiwan(x)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (Official(x) ∧ CitizenTaiwan(x)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(Vladimir) ∧ ¬ManagerAtGazprom(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ Official(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.
